body_status.title: Status
body_status.body_1:
Your fast has just begun. In these first hours, your body is still digesting your last meal and using glucose from the food you ate.

Insulin helps move glucose into your cells for energy, while any extra glucose is stored for later.

At this stage, it's normal to feel fairly steady.
body_status.body_2:
After the post-meal rise, your blood sugar starts moving back toward its normal range.

As digestion slows down, your body begins shifting away from incoming food and starts relying more on stored energy.

You may notice your hunger coming and going during this stage.
body_status.body_3:
By now, your blood sugar is usually back in a more stable range.

You might start feeling hungry, but your body still has plenty of energy available. It continues using stored glucose while your digestion finishes up.

This is the stage where your body begins preparing for a deeper fast.
body_status.body_4:
About 8 hours after your last meal, your liver begins using the last of its easily available glycogen stores.

Your body may start a process called gluconeogenesis, where it creates glucose from non-carbohydrate sources to help keep your energy stable.

This is your transition into fasting mode.
body_status.body_5:
Your glycogen stores are running low.
You may feel a little hungry, low on energy, or slightly light-headed.

This can also be a sign that your body is starting to tap into fat for fuel.

Fat cells begin releasing fatty acids into the bloodstream, where they can be converted into energy.
body_status.body_6:
Your body is now starting to use more fat as fuel.

As glycogen becomes limited, your liver begins producing ketones — an alternative energy source made from fat.

This stage is often called "fat-burning mode," and some people may begin to feel clearer or more focused once their body adjusts.
body_status.body_7:
The longer you fast, the deeper your body may move into ketosis.

Ketone levels rise, and your body becomes more efficient at using stored fat for energy.

During this stage, your body may also begin activating repair and stress-response pathways that support cellular balance.
body_status.body_8:
At this stage, your body may begin increasing autophagy, its natural cellular clean-up process.

Think of it as recycling: older or damaged cell components are broken down and reused.

This process may help support cellular renewal, metabolic health, and overall recovery.
body_status.body_9:
Around the second day, many people notice their mind feels quieter and sharper.

With ketones fueling the brain, focus can come more easily and mental noise may drop.

This is a common point in a longer fast. Stay hydrated, and end the fast when your body has had enough.

eating_window.title: Eating Window
eating_window.break_body:
Your fast is complete. Now it's time to gently refuel your body with energy and nutrients.

Start with easy-to-digest foods like **fruit, steamed vegetables, leafy greens, bone broth, or soup.** These can help your body ease back into eating and support stable blood sugar levels.

After fasting, your digestive system may need a little time to adjust, so try not to overload it right away.

To help prevent bloating or discomfort, avoid fried, greasy, or overly heavy foods when breaking your fast.
eating_window.nourish_body:
Now you're free to enjoy your meal. For steady energy and longer-lasting fullness, try pairing carbs with **quality protein and healthy fats.**

To keep your blood sugar balanced after fasting, avoid loading up on highly processed foods or sugary drinks.

Choose meals that feel satisfying, balanced, and easy on your body.
eating_window.next_body:
Your eating window is almost over. A nourishing final meal can help keep you full and support your body during your next fast.

Focus on foods rich in **protein and fiber**, such as meat, fish, tofu, fruit, vegetables, nuts, and legumes.

These choices can help you feel satisfied for longer and give your body steady energy as you move into your next fasting period.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.a_what: MochiFast is a friendly intermittent fasting coach that helps you build sustainable fasting habits with plans, reminders, and gentle progress tracking.
faq.q_start: How do I start a fasting?
faq.a_start: Pick a fasting plan that fits your lifestyle, set your meal window, then tap start when you're ready. We'll guide you through each phase.
faq.a_beginner: Yes. We recommend gentler schedules like 12:12 or 14:10 first, then you can step up when it feels comfortable.
faq.q_premium: What's included in Free vs Premium?
faq.a_premium: Free covers core fasting timers and basic tracking. Premium unlocks AI chat, all fasting plans, deeper insights, and extra coaching tools.
faq.a_history: Yes. Open Fasting History from your profile to review past sessions, streaks, and how your consistency has grown.
faq.q_cancel: How do I cancel a subscription?
faq.a_cancel: Manage or cancel Premium anytime in your App Store or Google Play subscriptions. Access stays active until the current period ends.

chat.reply_hungry_1: That hunger dip is so normal, squish. It usually passes in ~20 min. Try a big glass of water or black coffee first?
chat.reply_hungry_2: You've got this — and breaking early is okay too, no guilt. 💛
chat.reply_coffee: Yes — black coffee is fine while fasting. Skip cream, milk, and sweetener so you stay in your fast.
chat.reply_weight: Weight can stall even when fat loss is happening. Stay consistent a few more days and watch how your clothes feel too.
chat.reply_eat: Break gently: protein + fiber first — eggs, yogurt, or a veggie bowl. Save the heavy stuff for later.
chat.reply_default: Got it, squish. Tell me a bit more and I'll coach you through it. 💪

basics.title: What is intermittent fasting?
basics.subtitle: Simple answers for a healthier, happier you.
basics.quote: It's not about eating less, it's about eating at the right time.
basics.card1_body: Intermittent fasting cycles between periods of eating and fasting. It doesn't specify which foods to eat, but when to eat.
basics.card2_title: You still have an eating window
basics.card2_body: You can enjoy your favorite foods during your eating window, while fasting gives your body time to rest and reset.
basics.card3_body: Many people use intermittent fasting to feel more energetic, maintain a healthy weight, and support overall well-being.
basics.tip: Start gently and find a plan that fits your lifestyle. Consistency matters more than perfection!

during.title: What happens while you fast?
during.subtitle: A calm guide for the hours between meals.
during.quote: Hunger comes in waves. Most of them pass if you give them a little time.
during.card1_title: The first hours are the loudest
during.card1_body: Your body is used to a routine. Early hunger is often habit, not an emergency.
during.card2_body: Sip water through the fast. It keeps you comfortable and gives your hands something to do.
during.card3_body: A short walk or a few quiet minutes usually helps more than watching the clock.
during.tip: If you feel dizzy or unwell, end the fast and eat. A good plan is one you can repeat tomorrow.

eating.title: How should you use your meals?
eating.subtitle: Make the hours you eat count.
eating.quote: The window is not a finish line. It is where you refuel with care.
eating.card1_body: Open the window with protein, plants, and something you enjoy. Skipping straight to snacks leaves you hungrier.
eating.card2_title: You do not need to earn food
eating.card2_body: Fasting is not a punishment. Eat enough to feel satisfied, not stuffed.
eating.card3_body: Stop when you are comfortably full. The next fast is easier when the last meal was kind.
eating.tip: Plan the first meal before the window opens. Deciding while hungry usually means grabbing whatever is closest.

health.title: How does fasting fit a normal day?
health.subtitle: Sleep, energy, and mood matter as much as the clock.
health.quote: A fast works best on top of a life you can actually live.
health.card1_title: Sleep is part of the plan
health.card1_body: Short nights make hunger louder. Protect your bedtime the same way you protect your eating window.
health.card2_title: Move, but do not force it
health.card2_body: Light movement on a fasting day is enough. Save hard workouts for when you have eaten.
health.card3_body: Fasting should not be another thing to worry about. If a day is already heavy, a shorter fast is still a win.
health.tip: Pair the fast with one steady habit, like a morning walk or a glass of water. One anchor beats a perfect schedule.

tips.title: What should you remember?
tips.subtitle: Short advice from your fasting buddy.
tips.quote: Small repeats beat a dramatic first week.
tips.card1_title: Pick a window you already like
tips.card1_body: The best plan is close to how you already eat. Shift it a little, not all at once.
tips.card2_body: A plan you say out loud is easier to keep. Check in with yourself at the same time each day.
tips.card3_body: One broken fast does not reset you. Eat, rest, and start the next window without a speech.
tips.tip: Keep the goal boring and kind. You are building a rhythm, not winning a race.
